channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Case Study #01: Real-Time Sync Deadlock & Retry Storm in Commercial Unity WebGL (Analysis & Remediation)
item.description: A case study breaks down how a real-time sync deadlock and retry storm happened in a commercial Unity WebGL game and how it was fixed.

item.title: Setting a Frame-Time Budget for an Unreal Engine 5 Game: Eight Checks Before Your First Alpha
item.description: Small teams usually discover performance problems at their first alpha, so this article offers eight upfront checks that turn “it feels slow” into a frame-time number each discipline owns.

item.title: RAWG vs IGDB in 2026: which video game API to use, and when you need live player data
item.description: RAWG and IGDB are the two big game databases you'll meet when building a discovery app, bot or recommendation engine — which one fits depends on whether you need live player data.

item.title: Add Instant 'Game Feel' With This 6-Line JS Screen Shake & Hit-Stop Trick
item.description: No physics engine needed — six lines of canvas shake and hit-stop inside the render loop give a 2D browser game instant arcade-style game feel.

item.title: Binding of Isaac Dev Removes AI Music After Steam Review Bombing
item.description: Players will find out if a commercial game ships AI-generated assets — and hold the developers accountable, as The Binding of Isaac's creator just learned.

item.title: 3Draft : Game Engine Targetting System
item.description: The author builds a live space-station scene in 3Draft, his own browser-based 3D engine, and walks through the targeting system behind its LEGO-like assembly of low-poly scenes and characters.

item.title: Building a Reliable Gaming Setup Advisor: Rules, Data, and Honest Recommendations
item.description: A look at how to design a trustworthy gaming setup advisor: separate hardware specs from real in-game performance, be clear about what can and cannot be verified, and structure the recommendations honestly, with a PS5 advisor as the worked example.

item.title: I made an offline scope board for game jams: one HTML file, no accounts
item.description: A single-file offline planning board for 48-hour game jams — set the goal, budget hours, reserve testing time, with data stored locally and CSV export and PDF printing built in.

item.title: What I learned shipping a 31-game arcade in the browser with no engine
item.description: A four-file, framework-free, engine-free browser arcade with 31 missions and a 3D hub rendered by hand-written WebGL — the author sums up the pitfalls and trade-offs.

item.title: Five one-button games, one human finished any. Here is what broke.
item.description: The author shipped five single-file, one-button browser games in two months and reviews why almost nobody could finish any of them, and the mistakes made along the way.

item.title: No one is coming to help you in learning a Development
item.description: The author looks back on learning game development the hard way: after bingeing tutorials and learning C# for Unity, they still did not know where to start when actually building a game, a reminder not to stop at watching tutorials.

item.title: Automating Godot 4 GLB Asset Pipelines: Vertex Pivot Grounding, Colliders, Occluders & MeshLibrary Baking
item.description: A practical guide to batch-importing 150+ modular GLB assets into Godot 4, automatically grounding pivots, adding colliders and occluders, and baking them into a MeshLibrary for smoother level building.

item.title: NESkit Studio - a Fantasy Console for NES
item.description: A fantasy console built with C99 and cc65 for making real NES games, packing sprite and map editors, a sound effects maker, a music tracker and a code editor into one approachable toolkit.

item.title: GTA 6 goes gangbusters, Netflix Games layoffs and Pikmin Bloom's unlikely rise | Week in Mobile Games podcast
item.description: The 111th episode covers the week's mobile games news: GTA 6 going gangbusters, Netflix Games layoffs and Pikmin Bloom's unlikely rise.

item.title: Making a Game for Kids in the US: Eight Things to Settle Before Anyone Writes Code
item.description: Building a game for US kids means settling data, ads, store rules and readability for seven-year-olds before anyone writes a line of code.

item.title: Void Runner
item.description: An indie-made fast-paced 2D arcade survival game about dodging threats in the Void, with multiple modes, a shooting mode and a winter event, now playable on itch.io.

item.title: GTA 6 and the Open-World Streaming Problem
item.description: Drawing on two of Rockstar's technology leads, this piece breaks down how GTA 6 fits Vice City into console memory and a single frame budget, with a parallel to the same problem in web map loading.

item.title: The dials behind an idle game economy
item.description: An idle-game developer shows how to turn a hundred-plus economy parameters into a searchable, explainable operator panel, so live tuning no longer depends on memory.

item.title: My AI agents' Godot game drew trees and a town behind its planet; two fixes cut 3 ms of GPU time
item.description: In Planet Wanderer, a Godot game written by AI agents, trees on the far side of the planet were wasting 4 ms per frame; splitting trees into smaller pieces and adding a horizon-culling test cut GPU time by 3 ms.

item.title: Figured it was time to start sharing what I've been working on...
item.description: An indie developer decides to share their work in the open, starting with a Sonic 3 & Knuckles remaster — tackling character movement, terrain collision, and 32:9 ultrawide support.
